Let $R$ be a commutative ring ([[def-commutative-ring]]). An **$R$-algebra** is a unital ring $A$ together with a unital ring homomorphism

$$\eta_A:R\longrightarrow A$$

([[def-ring-homomorphism]]) whose image is central: $\eta_A(r)a=a\eta_A(r)$ for every $r\in R$ and $a\in A$. The induced scalar action is $ra:=\eta_A(r)a$, making $A$ an $R$-module and multiplication $A\times A\to A$ bilinear.

An **$R$-algebra homomorphism** $f:A\to B$ is a unital ring homomorphism satisfying $f\circ\eta_A=\eta_B$. Such a map is automatically $R$-linear. An $R$-algebra is **commutative** when its underlying ring is commutative.

Fix $r,n\ge1$ and use the independent units $Q,u_1,\ldots,u_r$ of [[def-hh-multiplicative-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]]. An **$r$-multipartition** of $n$ is a tuple $\lambda=(\lambda^{(1)},\ldots,\lambda^{(r)})$ of ordinary partitions whose total number of boxes is $n$. Its boxes are triples $(c,a,b)$ with $1\le c\le r$, $a\ge1$, and $1\le b\le\lambda^{(c)}_a$. Order the boxes within component $c$ by the transitive closure of $(c,a,b)<(c,a,b+1)$ and $(c,a,b)<(c,a+1,b)$; boxes in different components are incomparable.

A **standard multitableau** $t$ of shape $\lambda$ is a bijective filling of the boxes by $1,\ldots,n$ that increases along every row and column. Equivalently, it is a linear extension of this finite box poset. Write $\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)$ for the set of such fillings and

$$ \operatorname{res}_t(i)=u_cQ^{b-a}\quad\text{if entry }i\text{ occupies }(c,a,b). $$

The **generic content field** is $K=\mathbb Q(Q,u_1,\ldots,u_r)$, the fraction field of $R$. The contents of distinct addable boxes of any multipartition are distinct in $K$. If two boxes in one component have the same content, they lie on one diagonal; the right and lower boxes immediately between them are distinct required predecessors of the southeast box. Consequently, for three consecutive labels $i,i+1,i+2$ in a standard multitableau, the first and third contents cannot agree. In particular every pair of contents among three consecutive labels is distinct in $K$. If two boxes in one component have content exponents differing by $1$, then they are comparable in the box order, so interchanging adjacent labels in a standard multitableau never gives a content ratio $Q$ or $Q^{-1}$.

derivations.claim: The dominance inequalities are reflexive and transitive. If they hold in both directions, all displayed cumulative sums are equal; subtracting successive row cutoffs and then successive component prefixes recovers every row length in every component, so $\lambda=\mu$. Thus $\unrhd$ is a partial order. The tableau $t^\lambda$ is standard: its entries increase left to right by construction, and every box in an earlier row or earlier component is filled before every box in a later row or component, so each column also increases top to bottom.

Fix $\lambda$. If $\mu>\lambda$, the cell axiom applied to $C^\mu_{u,v}a$ puts it in the span of the shape-$\mu$ basis elements plus $A^{>\mu}$. Every shape in that expression is strictly above $\lambda$ by transitivity; hence $A^{>\lambda}$ is a right ideal. Since $*$ preserves each shape and $A^{>\lambda}$, $a x=(x^*a^*)^*$ lies in $A^{>\lambda}$ whenever $x$ does, so it is also a left ideal. The same argument with $\mu\ge\lambda$ proves that $A^{\ge\lambda}$ is a two-sided ideal.

The given basis of $A^{\ge\lambda}$ is the disjoint union of the shape-$\lambda$ basis and the basis of $A^{>\lambda}$. Linear independence therefore makes the classes of $C^\lambda_{s,t}$ a basis of the quotient $A^{\ge\lambda}/A^{>\lambda}$. No choice is needed because the poset and every indexing set are finite.

Fix integers $r,n\ge1$. Put $R=\mathbb Z[Q^{\pm1},u_1^{\pm1},\ldots,u_r^{\pm1}]$ and $p(X)=\prod_{a=1}^r(X-u_a)$. Let $\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{aff}}$ be the unital associative $R$-algebra on generators $T_1,\ldots,T_{n-1}$ and $X_1^{\pm1},\ldots,X_n^{\pm1}$, with central $R$-action, subject to

$$ (T_i-Q)(T_i+1)=0,\qquad T_iT_{i+1}T_i=T_{i+1}T_iT_{i+1},\qquad T_iT_j=T_jT_i\ (|i-j|>1), $$

$$ X_jX_k=X_kX_j,\qquad T_iX_j=X_jT_i\ (j\notin\{i,i+1\}),\qquad T_iX_iT_i=QX_{i+1}. $$

Here the braid relation is imposed for $1\le i<n-1$ and the distant commutation relation for $1\le i,j<n$. Define the **multiplicative cyclotomic Hecke algebra of level $r$ and rank $n$** by

$$ H_{r,n}=\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{aff}}/(p(X_1)), $$

where $(p(X_1))$ denotes the two-sided ideal it generates. The unit $Q$ and the quadratic relation make every $T_i$ invertible, with $T_i^{-1}=Q^{-1}(T_i-(Q-1))$. The cyclotomic relation also gives the polynomial inverse

$$ X_1^{-1}=(-1)^{r+1}(u_1\cdots u_r)^{-1}\bigl(X_1^{r-1}-e_1X_1^{r-2}+\cdots+(-1)^{r-1}e_{r-1}\bigr), $$

where $e_k$ is the $k$th elementary symmetric polynomial in $u_1,\ldots,u_r$. The presentation already includes inverse generators; this formula records that the quotient does not require a separate inverse parameter. For $i\ge1$, write $X_{i+1}=Q^{-1}T_iX_iT_i$ when using the recursion determined by the affine relation.

This is the multiplicative presentation. It is not the additive degenerate cyclotomic presentation obtained after setting a parameter equal to $1$ and changing generators.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $S$ a set. There is a unital associative $R$-algebra $R\langle S\rangle$, the **free associative $R$-algebra on $S$**, whose underlying $R$-module is free on the set of finite words in $S$ (including the empty word), with product given on words by concatenation and extended $R$-bilinearly.

1. **Universal property.** For every $R$-algebra $A$ ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]) and every map $S\to A$ there is a unique unital $R$-algebra homomorphism $R\langle S\rangle\to A$ extending it. When $R=k$ is a field and $S$ indexes a basis of a vector space $V$, $R\langle S\rangle$ reproduces the published tensor algebra $T(V)$ ([[def-tensor-algebra-of-a-vector-space]], [[thm-universal-property-of-the-tensor-algebra]]).
2. **Two-sided ideal description.** For $E\subseteq R\langle S\rangle$ the two-sided ideal $(E)$ ([[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]]) is the set of finite sums $\sum_sa_se_sb_s$ with $a_s,b_s\in R\langle S\rangle$ and $e_s\in E$.
3. **Quotient universal property.** If $\varphi:R\langle S\rangle\to A$ is an $R$-algebra homomorphism killing $E$, then $\varphi$ factors uniquely through the quotient $R\langle S\rangle/(E)$ ([[thm-quotient-ring-universal-property]]); the quotient is the presented $R$-algebra with generators $S$ and relations $E$.

In $H_{r,n}$ define

$$ L_1=X_1,\qquad L_i=Q^{1-i}T_{i-1}\cdots T_1X_1T_1\cdots T_{i-1}\quad(2\le i\le n). $$

Then $L_i=X_i$ for every $i$, so the $L_i$ commute and are units. For $1\le i<n$ they satisfy

$$ T_iL_iT_i=QL_{i+1},\qquad T_iL_i=L_{i+1}T_i-(Q-1)L_{i+1},\qquad T_iL_{i+1}=L_iT_i+(Q-1)L_{i+1}, $$

and $T_iL_j=L_jT_i$ when $j\notin\{i,i+1\}$. More generally, for every polynomial $f\in R[X_1,\ldots,X_n]$,

$$ T_if(L_1,\ldots,L_n)=f(s_iL_1,\ldots,s_iL_n)T_i-(Q-1)L_{i+1}\frac{f(L_1,\ldots,L_n)-f(s_iL_1,\ldots,s_iL_n)}{L_i-L_{i+1}}, $$

where $s_i$ interchanges the $i$th and $(i+1)$st variables and the displayed divided difference is a polynomial. In particular the cyclotomic relation transports as

$$ T_ip(L_i)=p(L_{i+1})T_i-(Q-1)L_{i+1}\frac{p(L_i)-p(L_{i+1})}{L_i-L_{i+1}}. $$

When $p(L_i)=0$, this gives $p(L_{i+1})T_i=(Q-1)L_{i+1}(p(L_i)-p(L_{i+1}))/(L_i-L_{i+1})$; the cyclotomic quotient guarantees this only for $i=1$. It does **not** impose $p(L_i)=0$ for every $i$.

derivations.claim: On the free associative algebra define $*$ by $r^*=r$ for $r\in R$, $T_i^*=T_i$, $X_j^*=X_j$, $(X_j^{-1})^*=X_j^{-1}$, and $(ab)^*=b^*a^*$, extending $R$-linearly. Word reversal is an involutive anti-automorphism, so this defines an involutive anti-automorphism of the free algebra.

The quadratic relation is a polynomial in one fixed generator and is fixed by reversal. Each braid word in the $T_i$ is palindromic, each distant commutation relation reverses to the same equality with sides exchanged, each relation $X_jX_k=X_kX_j$ and $T_iX_j=X_jT_i$ reverses to its equivalent reversed equality, and $T_iX_iT_i=QX_{i+1}$ is fixed because its left word is palindromic and $Q$ is central. The inverse relations reverse to the other inverse equations, and the cyclotomic relation $p(X_1)=0$ is fixed because it is a polynomial in $X_1$. Thus reversal sends every defining relator into the defining ideal. As the ideal is two-sided, it is preserved under reversal, so $*$ descends to an involutive anti-automorphism of $H_{r,n}$.

The quotient is generated by the displayed letters and $R$, so any anti-homomorphism fixing them is unique. By [F3], $L_j=X_j$, hence $L_j^*=L_j$. On words in the finite generators $T_i$, reversal sends a reduced word for $w$ to the reversed reduced word for $w^{-1}$; therefore $T_w^*=T_{w^{-1}}$, as for the finite reversal anti-involution.

Let $(S,m)$, $W$, $\ell$ be as in [[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]]; let $R$, $v_s$, $H$, $T_s$ be as in [[def-hh-universal-coxeter-hecke-parameters-and-presentation]]; let $T_w$ for $w\in W$ and the spanning statement be as in [[lem-hh-reduced-word-independence-and-length-multiplication]]; and let $E$, $P_s$, $Q_s$ and $P_w$ be as in [[lem-hh-commuting-left-right-hecke-length-operators]].

1. **The length-operator representation.** There is a unique unital $R$-algebra homomorphism $\rho:H\to\operatorname{End}_R(E)$ with $\rho(T_s)=P_s$ for all $s\in S$; it satisfies $\rho(T_w)=P_w$ and $\rho(T_w)(e_1)=e_w$ for all $w\in W$.
2. **Standard basis.** $\{T_w:w\in W\}$ is an $R$-basis of $H$: it spans by [[lem-hh-reduced-word-independence-and-length-multiplication]] and is $R$-linearly independent. Hence $H$ is free as an $R$-module and every element of $H$ has a unique expansion $\sum_wa_wT_w$ with $a_w\in R$ and all but finitely many $a_w$ zero.
3. **Faithfulness.** $\rho$ is injective.
4. **Base change.** For every commutative ring $R'$ and every ring homomorphism $\varphi:R\to R'$, the scalar extension $R'\otimes_RH$ is, as an $R'$-algebra, canonically isomorphic to the quotient of the free associative $R'$-algebra on $(T_s)_{s\in S}$ by the two-sided ideal generated by the images under $\varphi$ of the relations (Q) and (B) of [[def-hh-universal-coxeter-hecke-parameters-and-presentation]], and it is free as an $R'$-module with basis $(1\otimes T_w)_{w\in W}$. No flatness or freeness of $R'$ over $R$ is assumed, and no torsion-freeness or semisimplicity of $H$ or of its specialisations is claimed.

Let $(S,m)$ be a finite Coxeter matrix with presented group $W$, length $\ell$ and geometric representation $\sigma:W\to\mathrm{GL}_K(E)$ as in [[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]], [[def-hh-geometric-coxeter-representation-and-roots]] and [[lem-hh-dihedral-root-recurrence-and-root-sign]], and let $J\subseteq S$.

1. **Support and reduction.** For every $w\in W$ the set $S(w)$ of letters occurring in a reduced expression of $w$ is independent of the reduced expression, and every word in $S$ representing $w$ can be transformed into a reduced expression by repeatedly deleting two letters (Tits reduction, using only letters already present). Consequently
$$W_J=\langle J\rangle=\{w\in W:S(w)\subseteq J\}.$$
2. **Intrinsic parabolic presentation.** Let $W_J^\ast$ be the group presented by the restricted Coxeter matrix $(J,m|_J)$ in the sense of [[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]]. The canonical homomorphism $W_J^\ast\to W_J$, $s\mapsto s$, is an isomorphism. Hence $(W_J,J)$ is a Coxeter system, its intrinsic length function $\ell_J$ agrees with the ambient length $\ell$ on $W_J$, and $W_J\cap S=J$.
3. **Minimal coset representatives.** Every right coset $W_J a:=\{ua:u\in W_J\}$ ($a\in W$, [[def-coset]]) has a unique element $d$ of minimal length; it is characterized by $\ell(sd)>\ell(d)$ for all $s\in J$, and it satisfies
$$\ell(ud)=\ell(u)+\ell(d)\qquad\text{for all }u\in W_J .$$
Equivalently, every $w\in W$ has a unique factorization $w=u\,d$ with $u\in W_J$ and $d$ the minimal representative of the right coset $W_J d$, and then $\ell(w)=\ell(u)+\ell(d)$. By inversion ($w\mapsto w^{-1}$ preserves lengths and interchanges the two coset families $\{W_Ja\}$ and $\{aW_J\}$), every left coset $aW_J:=\{au:u\in W_J\}$ has a unique minimal element $d$, characterized by $\ell(ds)>\ell(d)$ for all $s\in J$ and satisfying $\ell(du)=\ell(d)+\ell(u)$ for all $u\in W_J$.
4. **Type A.** Let $n\ge2$, $S=\{s_1,\dots,s_{n-1}\}$ and $m(s_i,s_j):=3$ if $|i-j|=1$, $m(s_i,s_j):=2$ if $|i-j|>1$ (a Coxeter matrix of type $A_{n-1}$). Then $s_i\mapsto(i\ i+1)$ extends to an isomorphism $W\to S_n$ (the letters $1,\dots,n$ carry the library's symmetric group by the order-preserving identification with $\{0,\dots,n-1\}$, under which $(i\ i+1)$ is the adjacent transposition $(i-1\ i)$), and for every $w\in W$,
$$\ell(w)=\operatorname{inv}\bigl(\varphi(w)\bigr),$$

Let $(S,m)$ be a finite Coxeter matrix with presented group $W$, length $\ell$ and geometric representation $\sigma:W\to\mathrm{GL}_K(E)$ as in [[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]], [[def-hh-geometric-coxeter-representation-and-roots]] and [[lem-hh-dihedral-root-recurrence-and-root-sign]], and let $J\subseteq S$.

1. **Support and reduction.** For every $w\in W$ the set $S(w)$ of letters occurring in a reduced expression of $w$ is independent of the reduced expression, and every word in $S$ representing $w$ can be transformed into a reduced expression by repeatedly deleting two letters (Tits reduction, using only letters already present). Consequently
$$W_J=\langle J\rangle=\{w\in W:S(w)\subseteq J\}.$$
2. **Intrinsic parabolic presentation.** Let $W_J^\ast$ be the group presented by the restricted Coxeter matrix $(J,m|_J)$ in the sense of [[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]]. The canonical homomorphism $W_J^\ast\to W_J$, $s\mapsto s$, is an isomorphism. Hence $(W_J,J)$ is a Coxeter system, its intrinsic length function $\ell_J$ agrees with the ambient length $\ell$ on $W_J$, and $W_J\cap S=J$.
3. **Minimal coset representatives.** Every right coset $W_J a:=\{ua:u\in W_J\}$ ($a\in W$, [[def-coset]]) has a unique element $d$ of minimal length; it is characterized by $\ell(sd)>\ell(d)$ for all $s\in J$, and it satisfies
$$\ell(ud)=\ell(u)+\ell(d)\qquad\text{for all }u\in W_J .$$
Equivalently, every $w\in W$ has a unique factorization $w=u\,d$ with $u\in W_J$ and $d$ the minimal representative of the right coset $W_J d$, and then $\ell(w)=\ell(u)+\ell(d)$. By inversion ($w\mapsto w^{-1}$ preserves lengths and interchanges the two coset families $\{W_Ja\}$ and $\{aW_J\}$), every left coset $aW_J:=\{au:u\in W_J\}$ has a unique minimal element $d$, characterized by $\ell(ds)>\ell(d)$ for all $s\in J$ and satisfying $\ell(du)=\ell(d)+\ell(u)$ for all $u\in W_J$.
4. **Type A.** Let $n\ge2$, $S=\{s_1,\dots,s_{n-1}\}$ and $m(s_i,s_j):=3$ if $|i-j|=1$, $m(s_i,s_j):=2$ if $|i-j|>1$ (a Coxeter matrix of type $A_{n-1}$). Then $s_i\mapsto(i\ i+1)$ extends to an isomorphism $W\to S_n$ (the letters $1,\dots,n$ carry the library's symmetric group by the order-preserving identification with $\{0,\dots,n-1\}$, under which $(i\ i+1)$ is the adjacent transposition $(i-1\ i)$), and for every $w\in W$,
$$\ell(w)=\operatorname{inv}\bigl(\varphi(w)\bigr),$$
the inversion number of the corresponding permutation ([[def-inversions-inversion-number-and-sign]]). In particular a word in the $s_i$ is reduced if and only if its length equals the inversion number of its value.

Equivalently, every $w\in W$ has a unique factorization $w=u\,d$ with $u\in W_J$ and $d$ the minimal representative of the right coset $W_J d$, and then $\ell(w)=\ell(u)+\ell(d)$. By inversion ($w\mapsto w^{-1}$ preserves lengths and interchanges the two coset families $\{W_Ja\}$ and $\{aW_J\}$), every left coset $aW_J:=\{au:u\in W_J\}$ has a unique minimal element $d$, characterized by $\ell(ds)>\ell(d)$ for all $s\in J$ and satisfying $\ell(du)=\ell(d)+\ell(u)$ for all $u\in W_J$.

Then $s_i\mapsto(i\ i+1)$ extends to an isomorphism $W\to S_n$ (the letters $1,\dots,n$ carry the library's symmetric group by the order-preserving identification with $\{0,\dots,n-1\}$, under which $(i\ i+1)$ is the adjacent transposition $(i-1\ i)$), and for every $w\in W$,
$$\ell(w)=\operatorname{inv}\bigl(\varphi(w)\bigr),$$
the inversion number of the corresponding permutation ([[def-inversions-inversion-number-and-sign]]). In particular a word in the $s_i$ is reduced if and only if its length equals the inversion number of its value.

Let $n\ge2$, $R_0=\mathbb Z[Q,Q^{-1}]$, and $A=R_0[X_1^{\pm1},\ldots,X_n^{\pm1}]$ as in [[def-hh-type-a-weight-lattice-laurent-ring-and-divided-differences]]. 1. The $X_j$ commute and $X_jX_j^{-1}=X_j^{-1}X_j=1$.
2. $(T_i-Q)(T_i+1)=0$ for $1\le i<n$.
3. The $T_i$ satisfy the type-$A_{n-1}$ braid relations: $T_iT_{i+1}T_i=T_{i+1}T_iT_{i+1}$ for $1\le i<n-1$, and $T_iT_j=T_jT_i$ when $|i-j|>1$.

$$

$$

$$

Let $\alpha=(\alpha^{(1)},\ldots,\alpha^{(r)})$ be a multicomposition of $n$: each $\alpha^{(c)}$ is a finite sequence of nonnegative row lengths, and the total of all parts is $n$. Let $R=\mathbb Z[Q^{\pm1},u_1^{\pm1},\ldots,u_r^{\pm1}]$, and let $L_1=X_1$, $L_{j+1}=Q^{-1}T_jL_jT_j$ be the commuting Murphy generators of the multiplicative cyclotomic algebra. For integers $0=a_1\le a_2\le\cdots\le a_r\le n$, define
$$u_{\mathbf a}=\prod_{c=1}^r\prod_{j=1}^{a_c}(L_j-u_c).$$
For $b=\mathbf a+e_k$ with $b_c\le n$ for every $c$, one has
$$u_{\mathbf a}T_{a_k}\cdots T_1X_1T_1\cdots T_{a_k}=Q^{a_k}u_k u_{\mathbf a}+Q^{a_k}u_{\mathbf b}.$$
An empty string of $T_i$'s is the identity.

For a multipartition $\lambda$, let $N^{\unrhd\lambda}$ and $N^{\triangleright\lambda}$ be the spans of standard Murphy elements whose shapes respectively dominate and strictly dominate $\lambda$. The componentwise finite-generator straightening, the displayed shift identity, and the component coset expansion imply that these spans are two-sided ideals and that multiplying $m_{s,t}$ by $X_1$ has same-shape terms with the same first index $s$, modulo $N^{\triangleright\lambda}$.

Let $\alpha=(\alpha^{(1)},\ldots,\alpha^{(r)})$ be a multicomposition of $n$: each $\alpha^{(c)}$ is a finite sequence of nonnegative row lengths, and the total of all parts is $n$. Let $\bar\alpha^{(c)}$ be the partition obtained by sorting the parts of component $c$, and write $\bar\alpha=(\bar\alpha^{(1)},\ldots,\bar\alpha^{(r)})$. Define $u_\alpha$ by the formula for $u_\lambda$ using the component totals, let $x_\alpha$ be the sum over the row subgroup of the row-filled multicomposition tableau, and set $m^\alpha_{st}=T_{d(s)}^*u_\alpha x_\alpha T_{d(t)}$ for row-standard multitableaux $s,t$ of shape $\alpha$.

Then $m^\alpha_{st}$ is an $R$-linear combination of standard cyclotomic Murphy elements $m^\mu_{uv}$ with $\mu^{(c)}\unrhd\bar\alpha^{(c)}$ for every component $c$, and with $\operatorname{comp}_u=\operatorname{comp}_s$ and $\operatorname{comp}_v=\operatorname{comp}_t$. Define $u\unrhd_{\rm tab}s$ by requiring, for every label cutoff $m$, component $c$, and row cutoff $k$, that the number of labels at most $m$ in components $1,\ldots,c-1$ plus the first $k$ rows of component $c$ of $u$ is at least the corresponding number for $s$. Then the output tableaux also satisfy $u\unrhd_{\rm tab}s$ and $v\unrhd_{\rm tab}t$.

In particular, for a multipartition $\lambda$, standard $s,t$, and every finite generator $T_i$,
$$m_{st}T_i\equiv\sum_v r_{t,v}(T_i)m_{sv}\pmod{N^{\triangleright\lambda}},$$
with coefficients independent of $s$. Consequently $N^{\unrhd\lambda}$ and $N^{\triangleright\lambda}$ are two-sided ideals for the finite Hecke subalgebra.

Let $R_A=\mathbb Z[Q^{\pm1}]$ and let $H_n$ be the type-A Hecke algebra on $T_1,\ldots,T_{n-1}$ with braid relations and $(T_i-Q)(T_i+1)=0$. For a partition $\lambda\vdash n$, let $t^\lambda$ be row-filled, $S_\lambda$ its row subgroup, $x_\lambda=\sum_{w\in S_\lambda}T_w$, and
$$m_{st}=T_{d(s)}^*x_\lambda T_{d(t)}$$
for standard $\lambda$-tableaux, with the tableau action and distinguished representatives fixed in [[def-hh-cyclotomic-murphy-elements]]. Then the $m_{st}$ form an $R_A$-basis of $H_n$, $m_{st}^*=m_{ts}$, and the spans $H_n^{\trianglerighteq\lambda}$ and $H_n^{\triangleright\lambda}$ of shapes respectively dominating and strictly dominating $\lambda$ are two-sided ideals. For every $h\in H_n$ and standard $s,t$ of shape $\lambda$,
$$m_{st}h\equiv\sum_{v\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)}r_{t,v}(h)m_{sv}\pmod{H_n^{\triangleright\lambda}},$$
where $r_{t,v}(h)\in R_A$ does not depend on $s$. The proof is integral over $R_A$; it does not divide by $Q+1$ or assume semisimplicity.

Let $R=\mathbb Z[Q^{\pm1},u_1^{\pm1},\ldots,u_r^{\pm1}]$ and let $H_{r,n}$ be the multiplicative cyclotomic Hecke algebra of [[def-hh-multiplicative-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]]. For $w\in S_n$, let $T_w$ be the finite Hecke element given by any reduced adjacent-transposition word. Then

$$ \mathcal B_{r,n}=\{X_1^{a_1}\cdots X_n^{a_n}T_w:0\le a_i<r,\ w\in S_n\} $$

is an $R$-basis of $H_{r,n}$. With $K=\mathbb Q(Q,u_1,\ldots,u_r)$ and $f^\lambda=|\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)|$, the generic algebra is split:

$$ H_{r,n}\otimes_RK\cong\prod_{\lambda\in\mathcal P_r(n)}\operatorname{Mat}_{f^\lambda}(K). $$

For every commutative $R$-algebra $S$, the algebra obtained by applying $R\to S$ to the same presentation is free over $S$ with basis the images of $\mathcal B_{r,n}$; no flatness or semisimplicity of $S$ is required.

Let $f^\lambda=|\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)|$ for an $r$-multipartition $\lambda$ of $n$. There is an explicit bijection between **$r$-colored permutations** $(\sigma,\kappa)\in S_n\times\{1,\ldots,r\}^n$ and pairs $(P,Q)$ of standard multitableaux of a common shape. Its forward map scans positions $i=1,\ldots,n$: if $\kappa_i=c$, row-insert the value $\sigma(i)$ into component $c$ of $P$ and place the recording label $i$ in the new box of component $c$ of $Q$. Its inverse scans $i=n,n-1,\ldots,1$: find the unique component whose recording tableau contains $i$, delete that recording corner, and reverse-row-delete the corresponding box of its insertion tableau to recover $\sigma(i)$; the component is $\kappa_i$. Consequently,

$$ \sum_{\lambda\in\mathcal P_r(n)}(f^\lambda)^2=r^n n!. $$

Let $k$ be a field.

1. Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $M$ a free $R$-module of finite rank $n$ with basis $(e_0,\dots,e_{n-1})$, and let $v_0,\dots,v_{n-1}\in M$ span $M$. Then the coordinate matrix $A$ of $(v_0,\dots,v_{n-1})$ in the basis $(e_i)$ has a right inverse, $\det(A)$ is a unit of $R$, and $(v_0,\dots,v_{n-1})$ is a basis of $M$. The determinant is formed for $n\ge1$; for $n=0$ the module is the zero module and the empty family is its basis, with no determinant clause.
2. If $F\subseteq E$ is a field extension and $A\in M_{m\times n}(F)$, then the rank of $A$ over $F$ equals its rank over $E$.
3. Let $B$ be a finite-dimensional $k$-algebra and $N$ a finite-dimensional left $B$-module. A proper submodule has strictly smaller $k$-dimension, a maximal proper submodule of a nonzero finite-dimensional module exists by maximal dimension (no arbitrary Choice), and iterating produces a finite composition series of $N$ ([[def-composition-series-and-length-of-a-module]]); in particular $N$ has finite length.
4. If $S_1,\dots,S_m$ are simple $B$-modules and $N\subseteq S_1\oplus\cdots\oplus S_m$ is a submodule, then $N$ is isomorphic to a direct sum of a subfamily of the $S_i$, and $N$ has a complement in $S_1\oplus\cdots\oplus S_m$.
5. If $T:N\to N$ is $k$-linear with $T^r=0$ for some $r\ge1$, then $\operatorname{tr}(T)=0$ ([[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]).

Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $A$ be a unital associative $R$-algebra. A **cell datum** for $A$ consists of a finite poset $(\Lambda,\ge)$, finite sets $T(\lambda)$ for $\lambda\in\Lambda$, an $R$-basis $\{C^\lambda_{s,t}:\lambda\in\Lambda,\ s,t\in T(\lambda)\}$ of $A$, and an $R$-linear involutive algebra anti-automorphism $*$ satisfying $({C^\lambda_{s,t}})^*=C^\lambda_{t,s}$ and the following coefficient-independence axiom: for every $\lambda\in\Lambda$, $s,t\in T(\lambda)$, and $a\in A$, there are coefficients $r^\lambda_{t,v}(a)\in R$, independent of $s$, such that
$$C^\lambda_{s,t}a\equiv\sum_{v\in T(\lambda)}r^\lambda_{t,v}(a)C^\lambda_{s,v}\pmod{A^{>\lambda}},$$
where $A^{>\lambda}$ is the $R$-span of basis elements $C^\mu_{u,v}$ with $\mu>\lambda$. Write $A^{\ge\lambda}$ for the span with $\mu\ge\lambda$.

For multipartitions $\lambda,\mu$ of $n$ with $r$ ordered components, write $\lambda\unrhd\mu$ if for every component $1\le c\le r$ and row cutoff $j\ge0$,
$$\sum_{d<c}|\lambda^{(d)}|+\sum_{i=1}^{j}\lambda_i^{(c)} \ \ge\ \sum_{d<c}|\mu^{(d)}|+\sum_{i=1}^{j}\mu_i^{(c)},$$
with missing rows padded by zero. Write $\lambda\triangleright\mu$ when $\lambda\unrhd\mu$ and $\lambda\ne\mu$. The **row-standard initial multitableau** $t^\lambda$ fills component $1$ row by row, then component $2$ row by row, and so on, using $1,\ldots,n$ in order.

derivations.claim: For every $\lambda$, the componentwise and shift lemmas [F1]–[F3] give two-sided ideals $N^{\unrhd\lambda},N^{\triangleright\lambda}$ and show that right multiplication by any algebra generator preserves shape dominance. They also give the fixed-initial-row law for $m_{t^\lambda,t}$: modulo $N^{\triangleright\lambda}$ it is a linear combination of $m_{t^\lambda,v}$, with coefficients independent of the first index after left multiplication. To see closure under the full generator set, use the finite generators $T_i$ and $X_1$ from [F1]; the cyclotomic polynomial has unit constant coefficient, so $X_1^{-1}$ is a polynomial in $X_1$, while $T_i^{-1}=Q^{-1}(T_i-(Q-1))$ and the recursion expresses every $X_j$ as a word in $T_i,X_1$.

Let $U_\lambda$ be the span of $m_{t^\lambda,v}$ for standard $v$ of shape $\lambda$. The fixed-initial-row law shows $U_\lambda+N^{\triangleright\lambda}$ is a right ideal. For any $h\in H_{r,n}$ there are coefficients $r_{t,v}(h)$ such that$m_{t^\lambda,t}h\equiv\sum_v r_{t,v}(h)m_{t^\lambda,v}\pmod{N^{\triangleright\lambda}}.$ Since $N^{\triangleright\lambda}$ is a two-sided ideal, multiplying by $T_{d(s)}^*$ gives the displayed cell law for every $s$, and the coefficients remain independent of $s$. The generator-fixing anti-involution gives $m_{st}^*=m_{ts}$.

The row-filled multipartition $\lambda_0=(\varnothing,\ldots,\varnothing,(1^n))$ is dominated by every multipartition. Before the final component its cumulative counts are zero. At the first $k$ rows of the final component its count is $\min(k,n)$. If $i$ and $i+1$ lie in the same row of $s$ then $f_sT_i=q\,f_s$; if they lie in the same column then $f_sT_i=-f_s$; otherwise $t$ is standard and $$f_sT_i=\alpha_i(s)\,f_t-\frac{1}{[\rho]_q}f_s,\qquad \alpha_i(s):=\begin{cases}1,&s\rhd t,\\[1mm]\dfrac{[1+\rho]_q[1-\rho]_q}{[\rho]_q[-\rho]_q},&t\rhd s,\end{cases}$$ where $[-\rho]_q$ is the extended quantum integer of [[def-hecke-jucys-murphy-elements-and-q-contents]] and for the swapped tableau $\operatorname{content}_t(i)-\operatorname{content}_t(i+1)=-\rho$. No semisimplicity of $H$ is assumed and no choice principle is used.

Fix $r,n\ge1$ and work in the universal cyclotomic algebra $H_{r,n}$ of [[def-hh-multiplicative-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]], with parameters $Q,u_1,\ldots,u_r$, commuting Jucys–Murphy generators $L_i=X_i$, and finite generators $T_i$. For an $r$-multipartition $\lambda$, put $a_c=\sum_{d<c}|\lambda^{(d)}|$ and define
$$u_\lambda=\prod_{c=2}^{r}\ \prod_{i=1}^{a_c}(L_i-u_c).$$
Let $t^\lambda$ be the row-standard initial multitableau from [[def-hh-cell-datum-dominance-and-cell-ideals]]. Let $S_\lambda$ be the subgroup of $S_n$ that permutes labels within each row of $t^\lambda$, and set $x_\lambda=\sum_{w\in S_\lambda}T_w$ and $m_\lambda=u_\lambda x_\lambda$. The anti-involution $*$ is the generator-fixing map of [[lem-hh-cyclotomic-anti-involution-fixes-generators]].

For a standard multitableau $t$, use the right entry action $t\cdot w:=w^{-1}\cdot t$, where the left action applies $w$ to every entry. Let $d(t)$ be the unique permutation with $t^\lambda\cdot d(t)=t$. Standardness implies that $d(t)$ is the distinguished minimal representative for its row-stabilizer coset. For standard $s,t$ of shape $\lambda$, define
$$m_{st}=T_{d(s)}^*m_\lambda T_{d(t)}.$$
These are specified elements of $H_{r,n}$; this definition does not assert their linear independence or cellularity.

Fix $r,n\ge1$ and use the independent units $Q,u_1,\ldots,u_r$ of [[def-hh-multiplicative-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]]. An **$r$-multipartition** of $n$ is a tuple $\lambda=(\lambda^{(1)},\ldots,\lambda^{(r)})$ of ordinary partitions whose total number of boxes is $n$. Its boxes are triples $(c,a,b)$ with $1\le c\le r$, $a\ge1$, and $1\le b\le\lambda^{(c)}_a$. Order the boxes within component $c$ by the transitive closure of $(c,a,b)<(c,a,b+1)$ and $(c,a,b)<(c,a+1,b)$; boxes in different components are incomparable.

A **standard multitableau** $t$ of shape $\lambda$ is a bijective filling of the boxes by $1,\ldots,n$ that increases along every row and column. Equivalently, it is a linear extension of this finite box poset. Write $\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)$ for the set of such fillings and

$$ \operatorname{res}_t(i)=u_cQ^{b-a}\quad\text{if entry }i\text{ occupies }(c,a,b). $$

The **generic content field** is $K=\mathbb Q(Q,u_1,\ldots,u_r)$, the fraction field of $R$. The contents of distinct addable boxes of any multipartition are distinct in $K$. If two boxes in one component have the same content, they lie on one diagonal; the right and lower boxes immediately between them are distinct required predecessors of the southeast box. Consequently, for three consecutive labels $i,i+1,i+2$ in a standard multitableau, the first and third contents cannot agree. In particular every pair of contents among three consecutive labels is distinct in $K$. If two boxes in one component have content exponents differing by $1$, then they are comparable in the box order, so interchanging adjacent labels in a standard multitableau never gives a content ratio $Q$ or $Q^{-1}$.

Let $R_A=\mathbb Z[Q^{\pm1}]$ and let $H_n$ be the type-A Hecke algebra on $T_1,\ldots,T_{n-1}$ with braid relations and $(T_i-Q)(T_i+1)=0$. For a partition $\lambda\vdash n$, let $t^\lambda$ be row-filled, $S_\lambda$ its row subgroup, $x_\lambda=\sum_{w\in S_\lambda}T_w$, and
$$m_{st}=T_{d(s)}^*x_\lambda T_{d(t)}$$
for standard $\lambda$-tableaux, with the tableau action and distinguished representatives fixed in [[def-hh-cyclotomic-murphy-elements]]. Then the $m_{st}$ form an $R_A$-basis of $H_n$, $m_{st}^*=m_{ts}$, and the spans $H_n^{\trianglerighteq\lambda}$ and $H_n^{\triangleright\lambda}$ of shapes respectively dominating and strictly dominating $\lambda$ are two-sided ideals. For every $h\in H_n$ and standard $s,t$ of shape $\lambda$,
$$m_{st}h\equiv\sum_{v\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)}r_{t,v}(h)m_{sv}\pmod{H_n^{\triangleright\lambda}},$$
where $r_{t,v}(h)\in R_A$ does not depend on $s$. The proof is integral over $R_A$; it does not divide by $Q+1$ or assume semisimplicity.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $A$ a cellular $R$-algebra with cellular basis
$(C,\Lambda)$ and cell modules $C^{\lambda}$
([[def-cellular-algebra-basis-and-cell-module]]). For each $\lambda\in\Lambda$
there is a unique $R$-bilinear form
$$\langle\ ,\ \rangle_\lambda:C^{\lambda}\times C^{\lambda}\longrightarrow R$$
with
$$c^{\lambda}_{us}c^{\lambda}_{tv}\equiv\langle c^{\lambda}_s,c^{\lambda}_t\rangle_\lambda\,c^{\lambda}_{uv}\pmod{A^{\rhd\lambda}}$$
for all $s,t,u,v\in T(\lambda)$; in particular the scalar coefficient on the right hand side is
independent of $u$ and $v$, and $\langle c^{\lambda}_s,c^{\lambda}_t\rangle_\lambda$
depends only on $s,t$. This form is (i) symmetric,
$\langle x,y\rangle_\lambda=\langle y,x\rangle_\lambda$; (ii) associative,
$\langle xa,y\rangle_\lambda=\langle x,\,i(a)y\rangle_\lambda$ for all $a\in A$,
where $i(a)y$ denotes the right action $y\,i(a)$ of $i(a)$ on $y$, i.e. the
left action $a\cdot y:=y\,i(a)$; (iii) characterised by
$x\,c^{\lambda}_{uv}=\langle x,c^{\lambda}_u\rangle_\lambda\,c^{\lambda}_v$ for
$x\in C^{\lambda}$; and (iv) its radical
$\mathrm{rad}\,C^{\lambda}:=\{x\in C^{\lambda}:\langle x,y\rangle_\lambda=0\text{ for all }y\in C^{\lambda}\}$
is an $A$-submodule of $C^{\lambda}$, namely the kernel of
$x\mapsto\langle x,-\rangle_\lambda$.

derivations.claim: Work first over $K$. The cell forms are nonsingular by the separated supplier’s cellwise norm argument, before its faithfulness argument. If $\mu$ does not dominate $\lambda$, the product of a shape-$\mu$ Murphy element and a shape-$\lambda$ element lies in $H^{\unrhd\mu}\cap H^{\unrhd\lambda}\subseteq H^{\triangleright\mu}$ by [F1], so every shape-$\lambda$ element acts as zero on $W_\mu$. Order shapes by a linear extension of dominance. The action map $H_{n,K}\to\bigoplus_\mu\operatorname{End}_K(W_\mu)$ is therefore block triangular in the Murphy basis, and its diagonal blocks are invertible by [F4]. It is a linear isomorphism, proving faithfulness without the supplier’s semisimple-quotient inference. For standard $u,v$ of shape $\mu$, define the endomorphism $R_{uv}$ by $wR_{uv}=\langle w,f_u\rangle f_v$ on $W_\mu$, and by zero on other $W_\nu$. Nonsingularity makes these a basis of $\bigoplus_\mu\operatorname{End}_K(W_\mu)$. The action isomorphism just proved identifies these operators with elements of $H_{n,K}$. Thus the $R_{uv}$ are coordinates for $H_{n,K}$. Invariance gives $w(T_iR_{uv})=\langle w,f_uT_i\rangle f_v$ and $w(R_{uv}T_i)=\langle w,f_u\rangle(f_vT_i)$. Left multiplication therefore changes only $u$, right multiplication only $v$, and each changes its index only to itself or its standard adjacent swap; both directions of a standard swap have nonzero coefficients.

We need a comparison valid across shapes. Let $b$ be row standard with $i$ in an upper row and $i+1$ in a lower row, and put $b'=b(i,i+1)$. If standard $a\unrhd_{\rm tab}b$, then $a\unrhd_{\rm tab}b'$ and every standard swap $a'=a(i,i+1)$ also dominates $b'$. Only the cutoff $m=i$ changes. A swap raising $a$'s counts causes no problem. For a lowering swap, a failure at row cutoff $j$ would require $A_a(j,i)=A_b(j,i)$ while $b$'s swap does not lower its count at $j$. If both labels lie above $j$ in $b$, then $A_a(j,i+1)=A_b(j,i)<A_b(j,i+1)$, contradicting $a\unrhd_{\rm tab}b$. If both lie below $j$, then $A_a(j,i-1)=A_b(j,i)-1<A_b(j,i-1)$, again a contradiction. These exhaust the possible failures.

Let $B_r$ be the interval of labels occupying row $r$ of $t^\alpha$, and write $x_\alpha=\sum a_{uv}R_{uv}$. Fix a right index $v$ and an adjacent pair $i,i+1$ inside $B_r$. Comparing coefficients in $T_ix_\alpha=Qx_\alpha$, if $i,i+1$ share a column of $u$, gives $-a_{uv}=Qa_{uv}$; no other first index can contribute because $u(i,i+1)$ is not standard. Hence $a_{uv}=0$. If $u'=u(i,i+1)$ is standard, its coefficient equation has the form $Qa_{uv}=c_ua_{uv}+a_{u'}a_{u'v}$, where $a_{u'}\ne0$ is the seminormal off-diagonal scalar. Thus $a_{uv}=0$ forces $a_{u'v}=0$, and the reverse implication follows from the equation at $u'$. Zeros therefore propagate across every standard swap inside a block $B_r$.

Replace each label of $u$ in $B_r$ by $r$, obtaining a weakly increasing row and column tableau $S$. The standard refinements of a fixed $S$ are the linear extensions of the node-order posets in its equal-label classes. Any two linear extensions of a finite poset are connected by adjacent incomparable swaps: move the first desired element left across its predecessors in the other extension, all of which must be incomparable, and continue inductively. Here these are standard swaps of consecutive integers inside a block $B_r$. If $S$ repeats a label in a column, weak column order supplies vertically adjacent equal-label nodes, a cover pair $x<y$ in that class. A cover pair occurs consecutively in some linear extension: first extend the order ideal $\{z:z<y,\ z\ne x\}$, then place $x,y$, then complete; the displayed set is an ideal because $x<z<y$ would contradict the cover condition. This refinement has consecutive labels in one column, so step 2.1 and connectivity force every coefficient in its fibre to vanish. Therefore every supported $u$ refines a column-strict, hence semistandard, $S$.

A positive-integer column-strict tableau has label at least its row index. Put $b_j=\alpha_1+\cdots+\alpha_j$. Every entry $1,\ldots,b_j$ in a surviving refinement $u$ therefore lies in its first $j$ rows, giving $A_u(j,m)\ge\min(m,b_j)=A_{t^\alpha}(j,m)$ for all $j,m$. The right parabolic equation and the same argument give $v\unrhd_{\rm tab}t^\alpha$. Also choose the $k$ row labels whose multiplicities are the $k$ largest parts of $\alpha$. Column-strictness permits at most $k$ chosen labels per column, so their total multiplicity is at most $\sum_c\min(k,\operatorname{height}(c))=\mu_1+\cdots+\mu_k$. Thus each surviving spectral shape satisfies $\mu\unrhd\bar\alpha$.

Choose a reduced expression $d(s)=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_k}$. Every reduced prefix is a distinguished row representative: write $d(s)=ab$ with $a$ that prefix and $\ell(d(s))=\ell(a)+\ell(b)$. If $a$ were not minimal in its left row coset, some $y\in S_\alpha$ would have $\ell(ya)<\ell(a)$, giving $\ell(yd(s))\le\ell(ya)+\ell(b)<\ell(d(s))$, contrary to the minimality of $d(s)$. Hence $b_r=t^\alpha s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_r}$ is row standard, and each step moves $i_r$ from an upper row to a lower one. Apply $T_{i_1},\ldots,T_{i_k}$ successively on the left of $x_\alpha$. Their final product is $T_{d(s)}^*x_\alpha$. By steps 1.1 and 1.2, spectral indices initially dominating $t^\alpha$ continue to dominate $b_r$ at each stage; an unchanged index also works because $b_{r-1}\unrhd_{\rm tab}b_r$. The right index and shape do not change. Applying the right-handed argument along a reduced word of $d(t)$ now proves that the spectral expansion of $m^\alpha_{st}$ has support only at $R_{uv}$ with $u\unrhd_{\rm tab}s$, $v\unrhd_{\rm tab}t$, and shape dominating $\bar\alpha$.

Let $P$ be the finite set of pairs of standard tableaux of a common shape, ordered by $(u,v)\ge(s,t)$ when both tableau-prefix comparisons hold. This is a partial order across shapes: equality of all counts determines the row of each label, hence the row-standard tableau. Apply step 5.1 to every standard Murphy element. Its transition matrix $C$ to the spectral basis has entry zero unless its output pair dominates its input pair. Both families are bases by [F1] and step 1.1, so $C$ is invertible. In a linear extension of $P$ it is triangular, hence its diagonal part $D$ is invertible. Write $C=D(I+N)$; $N$ has only strict-order entries, so $N^{|P|}=0$, since a nonzero product would require a strict chain with $|P|+1$ elements. Therefore $C^{-1}=(I-N+\cdots+(-N)^{|P|-1})D^{-1}$. Every term has the same ordered-pair support, because the partial order is transitive. Each $R_{uv}$ thus expands only in $m_{wz}$ with $w\unrhd_{\rm tab}u$, $z\unrhd_{\rm tab}v$.

Substitute these inverse transitions into step 5.1. Every surviving standard Murphy term has $w\unrhd_{\rm tab}u\unrhd_{\rm tab}s$ and $z\unrhd_{\rm tab}v\unrhd_{\rm tab}t$. At the final label cutoff $n$, $w\unrhd_{\rm tab}u$ implies that its shape dominates the shape of $u$, so the shape also dominates $\bar\alpha$. This proves all assertions over $K$. By [F1] the unique standard-Murphy coordinates of $m^\alpha_{st}$ already lie in $A$; injectivity of $A\hookrightarrow K$ makes every coordinate proved zero over $K$ equal to zero in $A$. The resulting integral identities specialize under any map $A\to R$ sending $Q$ to a unit. No semisimplicity or quantum-integer division is required in $R$.
